newsitem.title: JAPAN: Summers says welcomes Japan commitment on recovery.
newsitem.headline: Summers says welcomes Japan commitment on recovery.

text.p: Deputy U.S. Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Tuesday he welcomed a commitment by Japan to take measures as needed to ensure a recovery led by strong domestic demand and to avoid a significant increase in its trade surplus.

Summers said his discussions with Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka, Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita and other senior Japanese officials on Tuesday covered the current outlook for the Japanese economy.

He said he expressed the desire of the United States that Japan pursue a supportive macroeconomic policy stance necessary to promote a strong recovery led by domestic demand and to prevent a resurgence in Japan's external surplus.

"Minister of Finance Mitsuzuka made it clear that the Japanese government shared these objectives and he committed to take measures as necessary to ensure a strong demand-led recovery and avoid a significant increase in external imbalances," he said.

Summers said three factors were necessary to restore domestic demand-led growth -- a macroeconomic policy framework that instills confidence in the Japanese economy and its ability to generate a recovery in domestic demand; the monitoring and implementation of structural liberalisation measures that help to create private investment; and working to repair problems in the Japanese financial system as quickly as possible.

He said he also discussed Japanese authorities' plans for deregulation and liberalisation of their financial system, the so-called "Big Bang", and said the United States was most interested in the proposals' capability to expand competition, promote greater transparency and see Japan create a stronger and more dynamic financial system.
Summers also said he urged Japanese authorities to move ahead quickly to clarify the specifics of the financial deregulation programme and to implement these measures as soon as possible.
He added that the Treasury Department and the Ministry of Finance would spend a full day on Wednesday in the first of a series of discussions on Japan's financial deregulation programme.

Summers also touched on a series of meetings held on Tuesday as part of the Six Markets Meeting of financial and central bank officials from the United States and five Asian economies -- Japan, China, Hong Kong, Singapore and Australia.

"This was a useful opportunity for us to discuss macroeconomic and financial market developments in our countries as well as the common challenges we face in building strong financial systems and capital markets," he said.

He said issues for consideration by the meeting were "less broadly political" than those considered by other groups. "I think this group can discuss a range of issues, relatively technical, financial issues that are of mutual concern."
He added: "I would just say that from our point of view, that problems in the (Japanese) financial sector are best addressed as promptly and vigorously as possible."
